businessModel: Donation-funded; no ads or paid tiers
updateCadence: Minor releases every few weeks, major (34, 35) a few times a year
summary: A single-process, highly customizable browser on the Goanna engine (a Gecko fork) that keeps the pre-Quantum Firefox interface and XUL add-ons. Free of telemetry and Mozilla-isms, but webcompat and security depth lag mainstream browsers.
bestFor: Fans of the classic Firefox UI and XUL add-ons
People wanting a non-Chromium, non-Gecko independent engine
notFor: Users who rely on modern web apps or WebRTC
People who need Netflix/DRM or WebExtensions

pros.title: Independent engine
pros.detail: Goanna is a separate Gecko fork, with new CSS and JS features still landing (Cascade Layers, WeakRef, URL.parse in 2026).

pros.title: Deep customization
pros.detail: Full UI customization, themes and personas, about:config.

pros.title: Low resource use
pros.detail: Single-process design needs little RAM; Windows 7 SP1 and Linux supported.

pros.title: No telemetry
pros.detail: No data collection or account tie-ins.

cons.title: Site compatibility
cons.detail: Newer sites that need modern JS/CSS or WebRTC (unsupported by design) break; a Firefox UA compat mode helps partially.

cons.title: No WebExtensions
cons.detail: Only legacy XUL/XPCOM add-ons from its own library; no Chrome Web Store or AMO.

cons.title: Weaker security model
cons.detail: No multi-process sandbox or site isolation like Chrome and Firefox.

cons.title: No DRM
cons.detail: No Widevine, so Netflix, Spotify web and similar do not work.

cons.title: Small team
cons.detail: Development depends on a few volunteers; binaries are proprietary freeware.

faq.q: Does Pale Moon support Firefox extensions?
faq.a: No WebExtensions. It supports its own legacy XUL/XPCOM add-ons from its add-ons site; modern Firefox add-ons will not install.

faq.q: Does Pale Moon run on Windows 7?
faq.a: Yes. Wikipedia lists Windows 7 SP1 as the minimum, with AVX required for 64-bit builds.
It receives regular security updates but lacks multi-process sandboxing, so it is less hardened than Chrome or Firefox.

switching.note: Imports from Firefox and other browsers; no extension migration.

spec.patchLag: Own security fixes; major releases every few months

jsSpeed: Goanna/SpiderMonkey fork, behind modern V8/SM on benchmarks
securityHardening: Single-process, no site isolation or modern sandbox
patchSpeed: Own security releases (35.0.3 on 2026-10-27); no upstream sync
lookCustom: Themes, personas and full UI customisation
extensions: Own XUL add-on library only; no WebExtensions
webCompat: WebRTC unsupported; modern sites break (Firefox UA compat mode helps)
openSource: MPL-2.0 source, but binaries proprietary freeware
